thread:
quentin: Support ticket — customer got a 500 on /v1/generate but they had exceeded a tenant quota. They expected 429. Posting headers for context.
maya: please paste the raw response.
quentin: ```http
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
X-Trace-Id: trc-203
X-Route: gen-ded-12
X-Quota-Check: deferred

{ "error": "shard_oom" }
```
elena: classic late quota enforcement. Gateway forwarded, route did admission and returned infra 5xx. Client sees 500 and assumes retry.
bryan: We've had similar threads; I'd like to propose a small but backwards-compatible versioning mechanism for client-visible outcome semantics. Two parts: 1) canonical outcome header `X-RI-Outcome` (values: quota_exceeded|rate_limited|auth|infra|unknown) and numeric `X-RI-Outcome-Code` (e.g. 429.1, 429.2, 500.3). 2) opt-in negotiation: clients can send `Accept-RI-Outcome: v2` to request gateway to apply outcome normalization for them. Without the header we preserve current behavior to avoid surprise for integrators.
maya: neat. That gives integrators control during rollout (they can opt in). For streaming we still need a sentinel pattern: final line JSON `{"ri_sentinel":true,"outcome":"quota_exceeded","code":"429.1"}` and close stream. Document that `Accept-RI-Outcome` also opts client into expecting sentinel events.
elena: telemetry: add metric `ri_outcome_total{outcome, outcome_code, origin, route}` and a derived `misattribution_ratio = sum(ri_outcome_total{origin=~"route|ingress", outcome="quota_exceeded", http_code=~"5.."}) / sum(response_total{http_code=~"5.."})`. Also tag logs with `ri_outcome` and `internal_cause`.
bryan: Console UX: add a small "Outcome contract" toggle per org: default off. If turned on, UI will show per-route outcome breakdown and surface "Accept-RI-Outcome" onboarding for SDKs with sample code. Copy: "Enable outcome normalization to make quota and rate-limit signals client-visible (beta)."
quentin: Rollout plan: implement normalization behind feature flag `ri_outcome_v2`. Start with gateway canary at 2% and a few opt-in customers that set Accept-RI-Outcome: v2. Gradually widen canary as SDKs update. Monitors: 1) 429 increase in metric (expected for opt-ins), 2) no rise in infra 5xx for non-opt-ins, 3) sentinel events appearing only for opt-ins. Pager if sentinel events correlate with >0.5% client errors for opt-ins.
maya: SDK guidance: for clients that opt-in, prefer `X-RI-Outcome-Code` numeric mapping over HTTP code. Provide snippets for python/js showing header negotiation and stream sentinel handling. Warn: do not retry immediately on quota sentinel; implement exponential backoff.
elena: tests: add e2e that simulates deferred quota in route. For opt-in requests assert gateway rewrites to 429 + headers for non-stream flows and emits sentinel for streams. For non-opt-in assert legacy behavior (proxy 5xx). Add CI check that gate keeps header names stable.
bryan: ops: make sure structured logs include both `ri_outcome` and `internal_cause` so SREs can find mismatched attributions quickly. Also add a dashboard tile: "Opt-in outcome vs legacy" to watch adoption.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feat/ri-outcome-v2 -> gateway-canary
quentin: I'll draft a short support message for affected customers explaining the behavior and how to opt-in if they want deterministic 429s. Keep wording actionable.
maya: one more naming nit: prefixing with RI (Redwood Inference) avoids colliding with other headers. Lock names early and publish in the changelog before broad rollout.
bryan: agreed. Also add a small migration guide and a sample nginx/express snippet showing how to add Accept-RI-Outcome when proxying requests.
quentin: ownership: @maya implements gateway translation + sentinel, @elena will add telemetry + dashboard, @bryan will draft console toggle + copy, I'll write the support follow-up and coordinate opt-in customers.
ops-bot: canary started: feat/ri-outcome-v2 at 2% traffic.
